subject: Retention & backup purge orchestration — MedTechCo DPA alignment
messages:

Cc: Legal Team <legal@medtechco.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Retention windows & backup purge — need narrower timeline and proof of erasure

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

Quick one as we prep for our compliance review next week: our legal team is pushing for a 30‑day purge window for ephemeral logs and debug traces originating from MedTechCo environments. Currently your documentation lists a 90‑day backup retention/restore window for snapshots and a 60‑day log archive.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide an operational plan to reduce backup purge timelines for MedTechCo to 30 days for the categories noted, and what that means for restore SLAs?
- We need verifiable deletion evidence (audit trail and a written runbook) that shows how a record is removed from primary storage, backups, and subprocessor copies (if applicable).

If a DPA amendment is necessary, please flag this and include a one‑page summary of the change. Legal is looped on this thread (cc).

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Brooks
Privacy Officer, MedTechCo

Subject: Re: Retention windows & backup purge — need narrower timeline and proof of erasure

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear asks. We can support a phased pathway to shorten the effective retention window for MedTechCo, but there are three operating constraints we should align on first:

1) Scope: which datasets to include (application logs, debug traces, KV caches, snapshots, full cluster backups). Please confirm the categories you want enforced to 30 days.
2) Restore SLA: reducing backup retention reduces the guaranteed restore window. We propose keeping a 7‑day rapid restore SLA for critical snapshots + a 30‑day soft restore (best effort) after the reduction.
3) Subprocessors & cross‑border copies: some backups are replicated to a small set of infra partners for durability — we will need to list subprocessors and what we can commit to remove on request.

I attached a first‑pass retention mapping (retention-mapping-v1.csv) that maps Redwood artifact types to purge timelines; this is meant to be a discussion document.

Next steps I suggest: internal alignment (cc'd) on feasibility + one‑page DPA delta for Legal to review. Karhik — can you sketch the deletion workflow and any constraints around snapshot pruning and immutable offsite copies? Kim — can legal confirm whether an addendum to the DPA will be required for MedTechCo's request?

I can then send a consolidated schedule and DocuSign-ready amendment for Elaine / Legal.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-17T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention windows & backup purge — technical deletion workflow

Team — technical constraints and proposal:

Summary: We can meet a 30‑day purge for application logs and debug traces by implementing a staged prune across three layers:
- Hot (primary) storage: immediate deletion on erasure request; we mark keys and evict KV cache; no change to latency.
- Warm (rolling snapshots): we maintain a rolling 30‑day snapshot window and expedite prune jobs that run daily; snapshots older than 30 days are queued for permanent prune.
- Cold (offsite/immutable): some cold backups are subject to cloud provider immutability for short windows (14 days) and then transition to lifecycle policies. For immutable snapshots we can request an accelerated purge but that requires subprocessor attestation.

Evidence we can provide: a deletion event (UUID + timestamp), S3 object delete-marker logs, snapshot prune job run logs, and a short script output showing object absence. For full legal attestation, we suggest a signed statement from the subprocessor(s).

Risks:
- Full‑text search restores for historical debug sessions will be limited to 30 days.
- If MedTechCo opts into cross‑region replication for resiliency, extra coordination with the region owner will be required (may add 48–72h to purge completion).

Attachments: proposed-prune-runbook.md (internal) — I'll push a cleaned version to the Drive link.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Distributed Storage

Subject: Re: Retention windows & backup purge — MedTechCo DPA alignment (proposed path)

Hi Elaine / MedTechCo Legal — thanks for patience while we scoped internally. Attached is a short proposal and the retention mapping CSV that reflects the changes we can commit to:

Proposal (high level):
1) Scope: apply 30‑day purge to application logs, debug traces, and ephemeral KV caches for MedTechCo tenant IDs X, Y, Z. Snapshots and cluster backups remain on a 30‑day rolling window with a 7‑day rapid restore SLA; cold offsite copies subject to subprocessor attestation.
2) Evidence bundle: for any purge event we will provide: deletion event record (UUID/timestamp), cloud object delete markers, snapshot prune job output, and a signed attestation template to be finalized with the subprocessor if needed.
3) DPA amendment: we recommend a short annex that: (a) defines the new retention windows for the identified artifact classes, (b) commits Redwood to evidence delivery within 5 business days, and (c) lists subprocessors that may hold copies beyond the primary window. Kimberly — I attached a draft change document (dpa-amendment-diff.docx).

If MedTechCo approves this approach I will:
- Finalize the annex with Kimberly and route for signature (DocuSign link to follow).
- Schedule an ops window (target week of 2027‑06‑01) to flip lifecycle policies and run the initial prune job for non‑critical artifacts.

Elaine — can you confirm the artifact categories and whether MedTechCo wants cross‑region replicas excluded from the 30‑day rule (i.e., keep longer for resiliency)? Also confirm that the Legal team can review the attached annex and sign off on the evidence requirements.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
